value.option_title: Ensemble size for rare extremes in a machine-learned weather ensemble
value.question: Does 10 to 1,000 AIFS-ENS members beat 50 for top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain probability forecasts, or does shared model error cap the skill?
value.hypothesis: More members keep helping: 1,000 members sample top-percentile tails far better than 50, so extreme-event scores keep improving [s_hens].
held_fixed: Variables: 10 m wind, 2 m temperature, 24 h total precipitation
Scoring: ERA5 1991-2020 seasonal per-gridpoint climatology, top-1% and top-0.1% thresholds
7 initialization dates, 50 IFS-ENS perturbed initial conditions x 20 stochastic draws each

predictions.if_lever: Skill on top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain keeps rising past 50 members: 1,000 members sharpen the tails and improve extreme-event scores.
predictions.if_not: Skill flattens near 50 members: members are exchangeable draws of one trained distribution, so shared model error caps tail sharpness and extra members add nothing.
predictions.decision_rule: if_lever if extreme-event Brier/fair-CRPS skill at 1,000 members beats 50 members by >= 0.01 and still rises to 1,000; if_not if the gain past 100 members is < 0.005 (flat within the bootstrap confidence interval).
predictions.noise_rule: Bootstrap over which members are sampled and over the 7 dates; a real difference exceeds the 95% paired confidence interval, and the fair-CRPS correction separates genuine tail information from finite-ensemble-size bias.
predictions.expected_why: A 50-member estimate of a top-percentile probability carries roughly 1/sqrt(50) sampling error that 1,000 members reduces threefold, and HENS showed huge ensembles sample tails better.

value.compute_tested_why: The test varies ensemble size (members per forecast), which is exactly what more parallel GPUs buy: more members in the same wall time.
value.scored_against: ERA5 reanalysis (independent truth the model was not fit to produce for these forecast dates) and SYNOP station observations, for top-percentile 10 m wind, 2 m temperature, and 24 h precipitation.

baseline.what: ECMWF operational AIFS-ENS: 50 perturbed members plus one control member

anchor.what: Reproduce the published 4-minute N320 member time and 38 GB memory; one control run must match ECMWF open data within ensemble spread [s_crps_paper].
anchor.published_value: 4 min per N320 member on A100 40 GB; 38 GB GPU memory
anchor.tolerance: timing within +/-25% of 4 min; 38 GB memory fits; control field within the ensemble's own member-to-member spread at each lead time (GPUs are non-deterministic, so exact reproduction is not expected)
anchor.independent_code: ECMWF Open Data AIFS ENS control member fields for the same initialization date, compared field-by-field

checks: One control-member 15-day forecast tracks the ECMWF open data AIFS ENS control within the ensemble's own spread.
Rank histogram of the 1,000-member ensemble against ERA5 is near-uniform (calibration sanity).
Fair CRPS at N=1000 converges to raw CRPS at N=1000 (size correction implemented correctly).
ERA5 climatology threshold yields ~1% of grid-point-days above the top-1% threshold.

phases.what: Set up anemoi-inference on one A100 40 GB, run and time a few members, verify 38 GB memory and ~4 min/member, anchor one control run to ECMWF open data.
phases.stop_rule: 10 GPU-hour time box, or stop when timing and anchor both pass.

gate.else: re-plan: reduce members-per-date to 500 and double dates to hold the budget

phases.what: Download ERA5 verification fields and compute per-gridpoint seasonal climatology thresholds (1991-2020).
phases.stop_rule: done when all 7 dates and climatology are local

phases.what: Generate 7 dates x 1,000 members (7,000 fifteen-day forecasts) on the 8-GPU A100 instance, streaming scores to disk.
phases.stop_rule: finish all 7,000 members, or the budget_usd hard stop

phases.what: Subsample each date's 1,000 members to 10/50/100/250/500/1,000; compute fair CRPS and Brier score vs N with bootstrap confidence intervals.
Verify top-percentile events against SYNOP station observations (stretch).

items.note: This is the plan's research question (framing). It asserts no factual claim, so nothing needs a source; the comparison of 10-1,000 vs 50 members is what the plan will measure.

items.page_quote: HENS precisely samples the tails of the forecast distribution and presents a detailed sampling of internal variability. ... For extreme climate statistics, HENS samples events 4σ away from the ensemble mean.
items.note: The factual claim '1,000 members sample top-percentile tails far better than 50' is supported: the HENS page shows information gain rises with ensemble size (7424 members reach ~4σ; Fig. 3 contrasts 50-member ensembles at ~2σ), and states sampling 4σ needs ~7000 members under a Gaussian. The quoted sentence appears in the abstract. 'Extreme-event scores keep improving' is the plan's prediction and needs no source. Note s_hens uses SFNO-BVMC (bred vectors + 29 checkpoints), not AIFS-CRPS exchangeable draws, but it still supports the general tail-sampling scaling.
This is the plan's predicted outcome if the lever holds. It is a prediction (what the plan expects to observe), which needs no source per the rules.

items.page_quote: The trained model is stochastic and can generate as many exchangeable members as desired and computationally feasible in inference.
items.note: This is the plan's alternative prediction (needs no source). The premise 'members are exchangeable draws of one trained distribution' matches the AIFS-CRPS abstract (s_crps_paper), which states members are exchangeable draws. 'Shared model error caps tail sharpness / extra members add nothing' is the hypothesis to be tested, not a sourced fact.
This describes what the plan will build and measure (running 7,000 AIFS-ENS v1 forecasts, scoring against ERA5, testing the 50-member threshold). No factual claim requiring a source.

items.page_quote: "AIFS-CRPS requires one single model evaluation to produce a 6 h forecast step for one ensemble member. This makes inference computationally cheap: a single member 15 day forecast is created in about one minute for AIFS-CRPS O96 and four minutes for AIFS-CRPS N320 on an NVIDIA A100 40 GB GPU, including the time spent reading the initial state and writing the forecast to disk."
items.note: The 4-minute N320 member time on an NVIDIA A100 40 GB GPU is stated verbatim on the cited page and supports the timing anchor.
